guide.title: Dartmouth Skiway, New Hampshire: the college's Lyme hill since 1956
guide.intro: Dartmouth Skiway's own "About" page describes the area as "Serving the Upper Valley since 1956," and its own website lists its address as 39 Grafton Turnpike Road, Lyme Center, NH 03769, with a copyright notice attributing the site to the "Trustees of Dartmouth College." According to Wikipedia, the Skiway is "descended from an earlier, smaller operation on nearby Oak Hill in Hanover," and opened in 1957 with a Pomalift on one peak; the Dartmouth Outing Club article on Wikipedia states that "by 1956, the Dartmouth Skiway was built at Holt's Ledge, replacing Oak Hill as the primary downhill skiing facility for the college."

sections.heading: The Dartmouth Outing Club and Holts Ledge
sections.body: The Dartmouth Outing Club, whose history is closely tied to the Skiway's origins, was established in 1909 by student Fred Harris to "stimulate interest in out-of-door winter sports," per Wikipedia. The Holts Ledge ski area, predecessor to today's Skiway, was formally dedicated on January 12, 1957, and its original base lodge, the Peter Brundage Lodge, was inaugurated on March 3, 1957, according to New England Ski History. Howard Chivers, a member of Dartmouth's class of 1939, served as the Skiway's first area manager; Donald Cutter, class of 1973, became manager in 1984. Dartmouth Skiway hosted the NCAA Skiing Championships in 1958 and again in 2003, per Wikipedia.

sections.heading: Lifts and lodges, six decades of upgrades
sections.body: For the 1960-61 season, a T-bar -- the Mueller T-Bar, per New England Ski History -- was added to serve a novice slope. In 1968, a new trail pod opened across the street on Winslow Ledge, served by a double chairlift, per Wikipedia. In the 1977-78 season, the Skiway's original Poma lift was replaced with a Hall double chairlift; in the 1985-86 season, a $1 million snowmaking system covering 43 acres was installed, per New England Ski History; and in the 1993-94 season the Winslow double chairlift was replaced with a Garaventa quad chairlift. Dartmouth Skiway's own website describes the McLane Family Lodge, completed in 2001, as "the centerpiece of the Skiway base area"; it won the 2002 Excellence in Architecture Award from the New Hampshire Chapter of the American Institute of Architects. In 2008, the Dupre family donated $750,000 to fund snowmaking improvements, per New England Ski History.

sections.heading: In Lyme
sections.body: The Lyme Inn's own website states it was "originally built in 1809" and currently operates as a bed and breakfast with nine guest rooms, five suites, and a standalone cottage. In the 1830s, stagecoaches traveling the old "Boston Turnpike" from Montreal passed through Lyme and stopped at the Lyme Inn, per Wikipedia's "Lyme, New Hampshire" article. The First Congregational Church's original 1815 steeple bell was cast by Paul Revere; it was later replaced with a bell cast by Henry N. Cooper & Co. of Boston, and the church's clock mechanism, from E. Howard & Co., strikes the hour, per the same source. Behind the church is a row of horse sheds dating from 1810; Wikipedia describes the 27 sheds standing today as "the longest line of contiguous horse sheds in New England, and possibly in the United States," each originally marked with its owner's name. The Lyme Common Historic District, encompassing the church and its surroundings, was established as the historic center of Lyme in 1781 and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on September 1, 1988, per Wikipedia's "Lyme Common Historic District" article.

faq.question: How old is the Dartmouth Skiway?
faq.answer: Dartmouth's own "About" page describes it as "Serving the Upper Valley since 1956." It descended from an earlier operation on Oak Hill in Hanover and opened at its current Holt's Ledge site in 1957 with a Pomalift, formally dedicated January 12, 1957, per Wikipedia and New England Ski History.

faq.question: Is the Dartmouth Skiway open to the public?
faq.answer: Yes. It is owned by the Trustees of Dartmouth College -- per the Skiway's own website copyright notice -- but operates as a public ski area serving the Upper Valley, including hosting the NCAA Skiing Championships in 1958 and 2003.

places.name: First Congregational Church
places.summary: Lyme's common-side church, with a Paul Revere-cast original steeple bell and a row of 27 historic horse sheds.
places.history: The First Congregational Church's original 1815 steeple bell was cast by Paul Revere; it was later replaced with a bell cast by Henry N.
